clue.text: Do all in one's power to achieve security

definitions.meaning: to make one's last possible effort, leaving nothing more to try
read literally: to slide home the bolt that fastens a door

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom comes from archery (loosing one's only bolt); the second reading takes it literally as locking up.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means using up every resource in a final effort, and literally means fastening a door bolt for safety.

clue.text: Slovenly behaviour of sons digesting recent new poetry

indicators.note: the two son letters take in the other pieces, as if swallowing them

parts.note: two sons, each abbreviated S
latter means more recent, nearer the end
lines of verse are poetry

explanation.surface: Boys take in fresh verse and display slovenly habits.
explanation.definitionFit: A slattern is a slovenly woman, so slatternliness is slovenly behaviour; a direct synonym.

clue.text: General dislike for ancient Greek theatre, say

indicators.note: the theatre word is spoken, giving a similar-sounding word

parts.note: an odeum was a roofed theatre for music in ancient Greece

explanation.surface: Widespread distaste for classical drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is hatred or disapproval felt by people generally, so it means general dislike.

clue.text: They emphatically identified writing in article on sprites

parts.note: the is the definite article
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
elves are sprites

explanation.surface: Fairies are named in a piece written about them.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the emphatic form of 'they', as in 'they did it themselves'.
explanation.definitionFit: The reflexive pronoun is used to stress the subject, giving an emphatic form of the plural pronoun.

clue.text: Knocked over container, an actor's source of fruit

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the container is turned upside down

parts.note: a tun is a large cask
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: An actor topples a tub, which yields fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked over' reverses the cask; the actor is Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree, the Victorian actor-manager, a figure older crosswords use freely.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazel or walnut is a tree bearing nuts, so it is literally a source of fruit.

clue.text: Way to capture foreign defence work

indicators.note: the way abbreviation goes round the other piece

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
alien means foreign

explanation.surface: A route by which to seize an enemy fortification.
explanation.definitionFit: In fortification a salient is an angle of works projecting outward towards the enemy.

clue.text: Revel in which Bess's man loses head

indicators.note: the first letter of the man's name is dropped

parts.note: Porgy is Bess's lover in Gershwin's opera Porgy and Bess

explanation.surface: A party at which a woman's partner is beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a wild party, so it is a noun for a revel.

clue.text: Cautious, taking wine before mounting musical

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine

indicators.note: in a down clue the show's name goes upwards, read backwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: A careful person has a drink before climbing on stage for a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A tentative step is hesitant and careful, so the word means cautious.

clue.text: Unable to concentrate as broadcast hit hard

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it
brained means struck hard on the head

explanation.surface: A radio programme is so violent that listeners lose focus.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone disorganised and forgetful is called this, so it means unable to concentrate.

clue.text: Gangster and president with the same characteristics

parts.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster
Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A mobster and a head of state turn out to be two of a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are similar share the same characteristics; a plain synonym.

clue.text: Entice agitated member to enter, having broadcast appeal

indicators.note: the limb word goes inside the shaken letters
stirred up, so the letters of the word before are shaken into a new order

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: Someone stirred up is coaxed into joining, being good-looking on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' gives TENIC; 'broadcast' sits in the definition here, not as an anagram signal, though it tempts.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who looks good on television has appeal when broadcast; a paraphrase of the adjective.

clue.text: The Vicar of Bray, or Norman Stanley Fletcher, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: the vicar of the old song who changed his religion with each monarch to keep his living: an opportunist
the convict hero of the British TV sitcom Porridge, literally someone doing his prison sentence

explanation.walkthrough: The Vicar of Bray is the archetypal turncoat; Fletcher, of the sitcom Porridge, is a prisoner serving time, a literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: An opportunist who trims his views to the times is called this, and literally it is a prisoner serving a sentence.

clue.text: Ruminative type providing material for Richard Rodgers?

definitions.meaning: a ruminant, an animal that chews the cud, here a male deer
Lorenz ... wrote the lyrics for Rodgers' songs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruminative' suggests a thoughtful person, but it means cud-chewing: a stag. Lorenz Hart was Rodgers' lyricist before Hammerstein.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is a cud-chewing deer, and Lorenz Hart supplied the words for the composer's songs.

clue.text: Was Kipling's Leopard originally this clean?

definitions.text: Was Kipling's Leopard originally this clean?

parts.words: Was Kipling's Leopard originally this clean?
parts.note: in Kipling's Just So Story the leopard began with a plain coat before he got his spots, so it was clean of marks

explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's 'How the Leopard Got His Spots' has a leopard that starts out unmarked.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleaned so that no mark remains, which suits the unmarked leopard of the story.

clue.text: Firmly decide to split up

definitions.meaning: to break something down into its component parts, as a prism does light

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to settle on a course and to separate into constituents.

clue.text: What a newspaper — now and then!

definitions.meaning: an exclamation in praise of a newspaper, using the name of the paper this puzzle appears in

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is an exclamation, 'Some Times!', praising the Times newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means occasionally, and split in two it praises the Times newspaper.

clue.text: Son tucked into excellent fish or cut of beef

indicators.note: the son abbreviation is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: top means first-rate, excellent
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A boy eats a fine fish or a joint of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' reads as eating a fish dish, but it is the container signal putting the son inside the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Topside is a lean joint taken from the hindquarter of a cow; an example of a cut of beef.

clue.text: Complaint about book? It's brilliant

indicators.note: the complaint word goes round the letter for book

parts.note: a lament is an expression of grief or complaint

explanation.surface: A grumble about a book turns out to praise it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent describes light that flickers and glows, so it is a literary synonym for brilliant.

clue.text: Thump new counter

indicators.note: the letters of the next word are made into something new

explanation.surface: Bang down a new shop counter.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce is to beat soundly, so it is a synonym for thump.

clue.text: Fuss preceding opening of boiler plant

parts.note: a pother is a commotion or fuss

indicators.note: the first letter of the word that follows is taken

explanation.surface: A commotion before the boiler is started up at a power station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory next to 'boiler', but it is a herb grown for the pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot-herb is any plant grown for cooking, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Old man ingesting a fighter pilot's sovereign remedy

indicators.note: the father word swallows the other pieces

parts.note: pa is father, one's old man
an is the indefinite article, a
an ace is a fighter pilot with many kills

explanation.surface: Dad swallows a pilot's cure-all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' must be read as its longer form before going into the father word; 'sovereign' here means supremely effective, not royal.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a cure for all ills; a sovereign remedy is an old phrase for one supremely effective.

clue.text: A, B, C, D, For G, for example?

definitions.text: A, B, C, D, For G, for example?

parts.words: A, B, C, D, For G, for example?
parts.note: the letters A to G, read as the names given to the pitches of the musical scale

explanation.walkthrough: 'For G' is the newspaper text for 'F or G'. The letters look like grades or a list, but each names a musical pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical pitches are named by the letters A to G, so each letter is an example of one.

clue.text: Shrub by Italian river, in group about small island

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
taken as written
a set is a group

indicators.note: the island word is turned round

parts.note: an ait is a small island in a river

explanation.surface: A bush stands beside an Italian river, among a party visiting an islet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns AIT (a river islet, also eyot) into TIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The poinsettia is a Mexican shrub with red bracts, sold at Christmas; an example of a shrub.

clue.text: One's rather upset, disposing of her bones

indicators.note: upset means overturned or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is I, and the possessive adds S

indicators.note: the letters of her are removed from the word rather

explanation.surface: Someone is quite upset at getting rid of a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposing of' removes HER from RATHER to leave RAT; 'upset' then rearranges IS + RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsi are the bones of the ankle, a plural of tarsus.

clue.text: Stylish character in Greek clubs

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
C is the card-playing abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A fashionable figure in Greek nightclubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means elegantly fashionable; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Unlike music you meet initially in Chopin's output

indicators.note: those first letters go inside the shuffled composer letters
Chopin's output is read as his letters put out of order

parts.note: the name with its possessive s supplies the letters

indicators.note: the first letters of the two words before are taken

explanation.surface: Music you first come across in Chopin's works is unlike anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'output' gives SPHONIC. The definition leans on the surface: Chopin wrote no symphonies, so symphonic music is unlike his.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopin wrote no symphonies, so symphonic music is the kind his output is unlike; a cryptic hint, not a synonym.

clue.text: Alluring female given name by male parent

parts.note: a sire is a father, especially of an animal

explanation.surface: A seductive woman is named by her father.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Sirens lured sailors with song, so the word means a seductive woman.

clue.text: Given time, office worker becomes a flighty type

parts.note: a secretary works in an office
bird is British slang for a prison sentence, from rhyming slang bird-lime = time

explanation.surface: Once given time, an office worker turns flighty.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'doing bird' means serving time in prison. 'flighty type' suggests a fickle person but means a creature that flies.
explanation.definitionFit: The secretary bird is a long-legged African bird of prey, so it is a type that flies.
